I am 65 this year, and I will keep my planting simple, steady, and low-risk. In Quzhou County, my land and my habits fit the usual wheat-maize rotation best, so I will not do anything too complicated. I will keep winter wheat on the main part of the land because it is stable, easy to sell, and I already know how to manage it. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same fields because that matches our local season, uses the land fully, and gives me a full year of production. I do not want crops that need too much fine management, too much labor, or uncertain markets. At my age and with my experience, I care more about reliable yield than chasing something new.

For management, I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed, because I want better emergence, stronger resistance, and more stable yield, but I will avoid overly expensive or fancy choices. I will apply fertilizer in a moderate way, not too heavy, because too much costs money and can lodge the crop or waste nutrients. For wheat, I will irrigate a few key times, especially around overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling if water allows. For maize, I will irrigate fewer times and focus on the critical growth stages. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing and is easier for me to manage. I will spray pesticides only when needed, mainly for common weeds, aphids, and diseases in wheat, and for weeds and corn borers or leaf problems in maize. My goal is steady production with work I can still handle myself.
